# Hotjar vs OpenReplay (2026)

## Overview
Hotjar and OpenReplay are two popular tools used for recording and analyzing user behavior on websites and applications. This comparison is beneficial for businesses, product managers, and developers who want to understand their users' interactions and identify areas for improvement. The core use case for both tools is to provide insights into user behavior, and the key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data or reduce costs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Hotjar offers a free plan and paid plans starting at $32/month, while OpenReplay is free and self-hosted.
* Data ownership: OpenReplay allows users to retain full ownership of their data, while Hotjar stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Hotjar is generally easier to set up, with a simpler installation process, while OpenReplay requires more technical expertise.
* Scalability: OpenReplay is designed to be more scalable, with support for large volumes of traffic, while Hotjar has limitations on its free plan.
* Feature difference: OpenReplay offers more advanced filtering and segmentation options, while Hotjar has a more user-friendly interface.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Hotjar | OpenReplay |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $32-$80+/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | AGPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | Approximately $1.28-$2.56 per user (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | Approximately $1.28-$2.56 per user (billed annually) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Hotjar:**
* Easy to set up and use
* User-friendly interface
* Offers a free plan
* Integrates with popular tools like Google Analytics
* Limited scalability on free plan
**OpenReplay:**
* Free and self-hosted
* Highly scalable
* Advanced filtering and segmentation options
* Retain full ownership of data
* Requires technical expertise to set up
* Limited support for mobile apps

## When to Choose Each
Hotjar is a good choice for small to medium-sized businesses or teams that want a simple, easy-to-use tool for recording and analyzing user behavior. It's ideal for those who don't require advanced features or scalability. On the other hand, OpenReplay is suitable for larger teams or businesses that require high scalability, advanced features, and full ownership of their data. It's also a good choice for teams with technical expertise who want a self-hosted solution.

## Migration Path
1. Export your data from Hotjar in JSON format.
2. Set up an OpenReplay server and configure it to import your exported data.
3. Install the OpenReplay tracking code on your website or application.
4. Verify that data is being recorded and imported correctly.
5. Configure any additional features or settings as needed.

## Our Take
OpenReplay is not yet production-ready for most users, as it requires technical expertise to set up and configure. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that OpenReplay has limited support for mobile apps, which may be a deal-breaker for some teams. However, for teams that value data ownership and scalability, OpenReplay is a clear choice, and we recommend switching from Hotjar if you have the technical expertise to set it up.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams with limited budgets who want a free, self-hosted solution
* Large teams with high traffic volumes who require scalability
* Businesses that value data ownership and want to retain full control
* Teams with technical expertise who want advanced features and customization options
* Companies that don't need support for mobile apps

## FAQ
### What is the main difference between Hotjar and OpenReplay?
The main difference is that OpenReplay is free and self-hosted, while Hotjar offers a free plan and paid plans. OpenReplay also provides more advanced features and scalability.
### Can I use OpenReplay with my mobile app?
Not yet, as OpenReplay has limited support for mobile apps. However, this feature is in development.
### How do I export my data from Hotjar?
You can export your data from Hotjar in JSON format using their API or by contacting their support team.
### Is OpenReplay suitable for small teams?
Yes, OpenReplay is suitable for small teams with limited budgets who want a free, self-hosted solution.
### Can I integrate OpenReplay with Google Analytics?
Yes, OpenReplay can be integrated with Google Analytics, but it requires some technical expertise to set up.

# Canva vs Penpot (2026)

## Overview
Canva and Penpot are two popular design and collaboration tools used by individuals, teams, and businesses to create visual content. This comparison is beneficial for users who want to switch from a proprietary, cloud-based solution to a self-hosted, open-source alternative, with the core use case being graphic design and team collaboration. The key reason someone would switch is to gain more control over their data and design process.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Canva offers a free plan and paid plans starting at $15-$30 per user per month, while Penpot is free and open-source.
* Data ownership: Canva stores user data on its proprietary servers, while Penpot allows users to self-host and retain full ownership of their data.
* Setup complexity: Canva has a user-friendly interface and is easy to set up, while Penpot requires more technical expertise to self-host.
* Scalability: Canva is designed for large teams and enterprises, while Penpot is suitable for small to medium-sized teams and individuals.
* Feature difference: Canva has a more extensive library of templates and design assets, while Penpot offers more flexibility in terms of customization and integration with other tools.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Canva | Penpot |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $15-$30/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MPL 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $15-$30/user/month (approximately $750-$1500/month) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $15-$30/user/month (approximately $3000-$6000/month) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Canva:**
* User-friendly interface
* Extensive library of templates and design assets
* Scalable for large teams and enterprises
* Integrates with other popular tools and platforms
* Limited customization options
**Penpot:**
* Free and open-source
* Self-hosting option for data ownership and control
* Customizable and flexible
* Suitable for small to medium-sized teams and individuals
* Limited template library and design assets
* Requires technical expertise for self-hosting

## When to Choose Each
Canva is suitable for large teams and enterprises that require a scalable, user-friendly design solution with a wide range of templates and design assets. It is also a good choice for individuals who want a easy-to-use interface and are willing to pay for premium features. Penpot, on the other hand, is ideal for small to medium-sized teams and individuals who value data ownership and control, customization, and flexibility. It is also a good choice for users who are comfortable with self-hosting and have the technical expertise to do so.

## Migration Path

2. Set up a self-hosted Penpot instance on your server.
3. Use the Penpot import tool to upload your designs.
4. Configure your Penpot instance to meet your team's needs.
5. Invite your team members to collaborate on your designs.

## Our Take
Penpot is not yet production-ready for most users due to its limited template library and design assets, as well as its requirement for technical expertise for self-hosting. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that Penpot's self-hosting option requires a significant amount of server resources and technical expertise. We recommend switching to Penpot if you are a small to medium-sized team or individual who values data ownership and control, customization, and flexibility, and are comfortable with self-hosting.

## Who Should Switch
* Small teams (less than 10 users) who do not need a wide range of templates and design assets
* Individuals who value data ownership and control
* Teams who require customization and flexibility in their design solution
* Users who are comfortable with self-hosting and have the technical expertise to do so
* Businesses who want to reduce their design costs and are willing to invest in self-hosting

## FAQ

Yes, Penpot is free and open-source.
### Is Penpot suitable for large teams and enterprises?
No, Penpot is currently more suitable for small to medium-sized teams and individuals.
### Can I self-host Penpot on my server?
Yes, Penpot offers a self-hosting option for users who want to retain full ownership of their data.
### Does Penpot have a user-friendly interface?
No, Penpot's interface is not as user-friendly as Canva's, and requires more technical expertise to use.
### Is Penpot compatible with Canva files?

# Canva vs Inkscape (2026)

## Overview
Canva and Inkscape are two popular graphic design tools used for creating visual content. Both tools cater to the needs of graphic designers, marketers, and small business owners who want to create professional-looking graphics without extensive design experience. The core use case for both tools is to design and edit visual content, and the key reason someone would switch from Canva to Inkscape is to have more control over their data and design files.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Canva offers a free plan and several paid plans, while Inkscape is completely free and open-source.
* Data ownership: Inkscape allows users to have full ownership and control over their design files, whereas Canva stores files on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Canva has a more user-friendly interface and is easier to set up, while Inkscape requires more technical knowledge and setup.
* Scalability: Canva is more scalable and can handle large volumes of users and designs, while Inkscape is better suited for individual users or small teams.
* Feature difference: Canva has a more extensive library of templates and design assets, while Inkscape has more advanced features for vector graphics editing.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Canva | Inkscape |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | Free / $15-$30/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $750-$1500/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $3000-$6000/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Canva:**
* Easy to use and set up
* Large library of templates and design assets
* Collaborative features for teams
* Integrates with other design tools
* Limited control over design files
**Inkscape:**
* Free and open-source
* Full control over design files
* Advanced features for vector graphics editing
* Customizable and extensible
* Steeper learning curve

## When to Choose Each
Canva is a better choice for large teams or businesses that need to create a high volume of visual content and require collaborative features. It is also suitable for users who are new to graphic design and need a user-friendly interface. Inkscape, on the other hand, is ideal for individual users or small teams who value control over their design files and need advanced features for vector graphics editing. It is also a good choice for users who are already familiar with graphic design principles and want a free and customizable tool.

## Migration Path
1. Export your designs from Canva in SVG format.
2. Download and install Inkscape on your computer.
3. Import your SVG files into Inkscape using the "File" > "Import" menu.
4. Familiarize yourself with Inkscape's interface and features.
5. Redesign and reorganize your files as needed to take advantage of Inkscape's advanced features.

## Our Take
Inkscape is not yet production-ready for most users due to its steep learning curve and limited support for certain file formats. One specific technical limitation worth knowing before switching is that Inkscape has limited support for raster graphics editing. However, for users who value control over their design files and need advanced features for vector graphics editing, Inkscape is a clear choice. We recommend switching to Inkscape if you are an individual user or small team with basic design needs and do not require collaborative features.

## Who Should Switch
* Solo graphic designers who need advanced features for vector graphics editing
* Small teams of 2-5 users who value control over their design files
* Users who do not need collaborative features or a large library of templates
* Individuals who are already familiar with graphic design principles and want a free and customizable tool
* Teams who are looking for a self-hosted solution and have the technical expertise to set it up

## FAQ
### Can I use Inkscape for free?
Yes, Inkscape is completely free and open-source. You can download and use it without paying any fees.
### Is Inkscape easy to use?
No, Inkscape has a steeper learning curve compared to Canva. It requires more technical knowledge and setup.
### Can I import my Canva designs into Inkscape?
Yes, you can import your Canva designs into Inkscape by exporting them in SVG format and then importing them into Inkscape.
### Does Inkscape have collaborative features?
No, Inkscape does not have built-in collaborative features like Canva. However, you can use other tools and workflows to collaborate with your team.
### Is Inkscape suitable for large teams?
No, Inkscape is not yet suitable for large teams due to its limited scalability and lack of collaborative features.

title: Sketch vs Penpot
comparison_markdown:
# Sketch vs Penpot

## Overview

Mac-only UI design tool popular with product designers. is a popular proprietary tool in the design space. Penpot is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Sketch costs $9-$20/user/month; Penpot is Free
- **License**: Sketch is Proprietary; Penpot is MPL 2.0
- **Data ownership**: Penpot can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Penpot eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Penpot has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Sketch | Penpot |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $9-$20/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | MPL 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$450/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$1,800/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Sketch

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Penpot

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [penpot/penpot](https://github.com/penpot/penpot) * ~33k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Sketch if:** Sketch is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Penpot if:** Penpot is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Sketch in its standard export format, review Penpot import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Penpot is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Sketch tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Penpot instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Sketch, switching to self-hosted Penpot will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Sketch until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Sketch paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Penpot free to use?
Yes. Penpot is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Sketch to Penpot?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Sketch data, follow the Penpot import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Penpot get regular updates?
Yes. Penpot has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Penpot without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Penpot development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Sketch](https://sketch.com) and [Penpot](https://penpot.app) before making decisions.*
meta_description: Penpot is a free, self-hosted alternative to Sketch. Compare pricing, features, and migration steps. See full comparison.

# Adobe Illustrator vs Inkscape (2026)

## Overview
Adobe Illustrator and Inkscape are both vector graphics editors used for creating and editing visual content such as logos, icons, and graphics. This comparison benefits graphic designers, artists, and businesses looking to switch from a paid tool to a free and open-source alternative. The core use case for both tools is professional-grade vector graphics editing, and the key reason someone would switch is to reduce costs while maintaining similar functionality.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Adobe Illustrator is a paid tool with a monthly subscription, while Inkscape is completely free.
* Data ownership: Adobe Illustrator stores files in a proprietary format, whereas Inkscape uses the open SVG format.
* Setup complexity: Adobe Illustrator requires a more complex setup process, including installing and configuring the software, while Inkscape has a simpler installation process.
* Scalability: Adobe Illustrator is designed for large-scale enterprise use, while Inkscape is better suited for individual users or small teams.
* Feature difference: Adobe Illustrator has a more advanced and comprehensive set of features, including 3D graphics and advanced typography, whereas Inkscape has a more limited feature set but is still highly capable.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Adobe Illustrator | Inkscape |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $20.99-$54.99/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $1049.50-$2749.50/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $4199.80-$10999.80/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Adobe Illustrator:**
* Advanced and comprehensive set of features
* Industry-standard tool with wide compatibility
* Regularly updated with new features and improvements
* Large community of users and developers
* Steep learning curve for beginners
**Inkscape:**
* Completely free and open-source
* Highly capable and feature-rich
* Cross-platform compatibility
* Active community of developers and users
* Limited support for certain file formats

## When to Choose Each
Adobe Illustrator is the better choice for large enterprises, professional graphic design teams, and those who require advanced features and industry-standard compatibility. Inkscape, on the other hand, is ideal for individual users, small teams, and those on a tight budget who still need a powerful and feature-rich vector graphics editor.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Adobe Illustrator files in the SVG format.
2. Install Inkscape on your computer and launch the application.

# Adobe Premiere Pro vs Kdenlive (2026)

## Overview
Adobe Premiere Pro and Kdenlive are two video editing software tools used for creating and editing professional-looking videos. This comparison benefits individuals and teams looking to switch from a paid, proprietary solution to a free, open-source alternative, with the core use case being video editing and the key reason to switch being cost savings.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Adobe Premiere Pro is a paid software with a monthly subscription, while Kdenlive is free and open-source.
* Data ownership: With Kdenlive, users have full control over their data, whereas Adobe Premiere Pro stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Kdenlive has a steeper learning curve due to its open-source nature, while Adobe Premiere Pro has a more user-friendly interface.
* Scalability: Adobe Premiere Pro is more scalable, supporting larger teams and projects, while Kdenlive is better suited for smaller teams and individual users.
* Multi-camera editing: Adobe Premiere Pro has a more advanced multi-camera editing feature, while Kdenlive's multi-camera editing is more basic.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Adobe Premiere Pro | Kdenlive |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $20.99-$54.99/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $1049.50-$2749.50/month | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | $4199-$10,999/month | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons
**Adobe Premiere Pro:**
* Advanced multi-camera editing feature
* User-friendly interface
* Scalable for large teams and projects
* Integration with other Adobe tools
* Regular updates and support
* Limited control over data ownership
* Expensive for large teams
* Limited flexibility in terms of customization
* Requires subscription
* Not self-hosting available

**Kdenlive:**
* Free and open-source
* Full control over data ownership
* Customizable and flexible
* Self-hosting available
* Regular updates and community support
* Steeper learning curve
* Limited scalability for large teams
* Basic multi-camera editing feature
* Limited integration with other tools

## When to Choose Each
Adobe Premiere Pro is the better choice for large teams and projects that require advanced features, scalability, and integration with other Adobe tools. It is also suitable for users who are already familiar with the Adobe ecosystem and prefer a user-friendly interface. On the other hand, Kdenlive is the better choice for individual users, small teams, or those on a tight budget who value data ownership and customization.

Kdenlive is also suitable for users who are comfortable with a steeper learning curve and are looking for a free, open-source alternative to proprietary video editing software. Additionally, Kdenlive is a good choice for users who require self-hosting and full control over their data.

## Migration Path
1. Export your Adobe Premiere Pro project as an EDL (Edit Decision List) file.
2. Import the EDL file into Kdenlive using the "Import" feature.
3. Adjust the project settings and preferences in Kdenlive to match your Adobe Premiere Pro project.
4. Re-link your media files and re-apply any effects or transitions.
5. Test and render your project in Kdenlive to ensure compatibility and quality.

## Our Take
Kdenlive is not yet production-ready for most users, as it still lacks some of the advanced features and polish of Adobe Premiere Pro. One specific technical limitation worth knowing is that Kdenlive's color grading tools are not as advanced as those in Adobe Premiere Pro. However, for users who value data ownership, customization, and cost savings, Kdenlive is a viable alternative, and we recommend switching to Kdenlive if you are an individual user or a small team with basic video editing needs.

## Who Should Switch
* Individual users who only need basic video editing features
* Small teams with limited budgets and simple video editing needs
* Users who require self-hosting and full control over their data
* Teams who do not need advanced multi-camera editing features
* Users who are comfortable with a steeper learning curve and customization

## FAQ
### Can I import Adobe Premiere Pro projects into Kdenlive?
Yes, you can import Adobe Premiere Pro projects into Kdenlive using the EDL file format. However, some features and effects may not be compatible.

### Is Kdenlive free?
Yes, Kdenlive is completely free and open-source, with no subscription or licensing fees.

### Does Kdenlive support 4K video editing?
Yes, Kdenlive supports 4K video editing, as well as other high-resolution formats.

Yes, Kdenlive is available for Mac, Windows, and Linux platforms.

comparison_markdown:
# Figma vs Inkscape

## Overview

Browser-based collaborative design and prototyping tool. is a popular proprietary tool in the design space. Inkscape is a free, open-source alternative that gives organizations complete control over their data and deployment.

## Key Differences

- **Cost**: Figma costs $12-$75/user/month; Inkscape is Free
- **License**: Figma is Proprietary; Inkscape is GPL 3.0
- **Data ownership**: Inkscape can be self-hosted so your data stays on infrastructure you control
- **Vendor lock-in**: Inkscape eliminates dependency on a single commercial vendor
- **Community**: Inkscape has an active open-source community contributing features and fixes

## Pricing Comparison

| Aspect | Figma | Inkscape |
|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Base pricing | $12-$75/user/month | Free |
| License | Proprietary | GPL 3.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Cost at 50 users | ~$600/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Cost at 200 users | ~$2,400/month | $0/month (self-hosted) |
| Vendor lock-in | High | None |

## Pros and Cons

### Figma

**Pros:**
- Polished, professionally designed user interface
- Large ecosystem of official integrations
- Managed infrastructure with no server maintenance required
- Enterprise SLA and dedicated support available
- Mobile apps are well-maintained and reliable

**Cons:**
- Significant per-user monthly cost that scales linearly with team size
- Your data is stored on the vendor infrastructure
- No ability to inspect or modify the source code
- Feature roadmap controlled entirely by the vendor
- Risk of pricing changes, acquisition, or discontinuation

### Inkscape

**Pros:**
- Free to self-host with costs only for server infrastructure
- Complete data ownership and privacy control
- Source code is auditable and modifiable
- Active open-source community
- No vendor lock-in or risk of sudden pricing changes
> GitHub: [inkscape/inkscape](https://github.com/inkscape/inkscape) * ~4k stars

**Cons:**
- Requires technical knowledge to self-host and maintain
- May lack some advanced features found in the proprietary version
- Support relies on community forums rather than a paid helpdesk
- UI polish may lag behind the proprietary tool
- You are responsible for updates, backups, and security patches

## When to Choose Each

**Choose Figma if:** Figma is the right choice when you need the most polished user experience, the broadest integration ecosystem, and professional support with SLA guarantees.

**Choose Inkscape if:** Inkscape is ideal for privacy-conscious teams, organizations with strict data sovereignty requirements, or anyone wanting to eliminate per-seat subscription costs.

## Migration Path

Export your data from Figma in its standard export format, review Inkscape import documentation, and plan a pilot period where both tools run in parallel.

## Our Take

Inkscape is production-ready for most teams willing to invest a few hours in setup. The self-hosted version gives you identical or better functionality to the paid Figma tiers, with no recurring per-seat cost.

The main technical limitation worth knowing: you are responsible for your own backups, updates, and uptime. If your server goes down, so does your Inkscape instance. Plan for this with automated backups and a monitoring alert.

Our recommendation: if your team has at least one developer and you are paying more than $100/month for Figma, switching to self-hosted Inkscape will pay for itself within the first month. If nobody on your team is comfortable with Linux or Docker, stay on Figma until you have that resource.

## Who Should Switch

- Startups under 20 people paying per-seat fees they cannot yet justify
- Dev teams who already self-host other tools and have the ops knowledge
- Organizations in jurisdictions with strict data residency requirements
- Teams who have evaluated Figma paid features and only use the basics
- Founders and solopreneurs who want the functionality without the subscription

## FAQ

### Is Inkscape free to use?
Yes. Inkscape is free to self-host. Your only cost is the server, typically $6-$12/month on a VPS provider like DigitalOcean or Vultr.

### How hard is it to migrate from Figma to Inkscape?
For most teams, migration takes 2-4 hours. Export your Figma data, follow the Inkscape import guide, and test with a small group before switching everyone over.

### Does Inkscape get regular updates?
Yes. Inkscape has an active open-source community with regular releases. Check the GitHub repository for release frequency.

### Can I use Inkscape without technical knowledge?
You need basic comfort with a VPS and command line. If that feels unfamiliar, there are managed hosting options that handle the server for you at a modest cost.

### What happens if Inkscape development stops?
Because the source code is open, you can continue running whatever version you have indefinitely. You can also fork the project or switch to another tool at your own pace — no vendor can shut off your instance.

---
*Data sourced June 2026. Pricing and features change. Verify at [Figma](https://figma.com) and [Inkscape](https://inkscape.org) before making decisions.*
